transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s mostly these nagging thoughts at work. I’ll finish a layout or send something to a client, and then I keep thinking maybe I missed some tiny mistake, or sent the wrong version. Even when I can tell it’s probably fine, I can’t really let it go.
Do these thoughts cause you a lot of stress or interfere with your ability to get things done at work?

Yeah… somewhat. I mean, I’m still getting the work done, mostly. But I’ve been slipping on some internal deadlines because I keep checking things, and I’ve noticed I play it safer with designs now. I worry that if I miss something, it’ll hurt my chances of moving up, like toward a creative director role.

When you have these thoughts about mistakes, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly—like checking your work over and over, going back to emails after you’ve sent them, or mentally reviewing things—to try to reduce the anxiety or prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah… I do check. Before I submit something, I’ll reopen the file and look at the layers again, compare things, re-save it… sometimes I sort of run through the design choices in my head one more time. It’s not like it takes up my whole day, but it definitely slows me down. And I think it makes me less… loose with the creative part.

Do these thoughts about mistakes ever lead you to do something specific over and over again, like rechecking files, redoing parts of your work, or following certain mental rituals, even if you know it might be unnecessary?

Yes… I guess so. Before I submit something, I’ll usually reopen the file, check the layers against each other, save it again… and then sometimes I sort of mentally go through why I made each design choice. It doesn’t take over the whole day, but it slows me down, and I feel less free with the work.
